name: ZWF World Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served World Title page runs a "Last 5 title changes" ledger across five reigns from 1 July to 12 August 2002: Brock Lesnar filled a vacancy by defeating Jerry Lynn by default, The Undertaker beat Lesnar eighteen days later, Sting beat Undertaker, the belt sat vacant again until Jerry Lynn beat Lesnar to reclaim it, and Undertaker beat Lynn for his second reign — the fed's own current champion as of its latest content. A served Summerslam broadcast separately stages Undertaker defending the belt in a steel cage against Triple H, winning clean before Sting attacks him after the bell and drapes the title over him — an echo of the ledger's own Sting reign, never explicitly confirmed as the same event.

name: ZWF Light Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Chris Jericho carried the belt into ZWF Summerslam with no surviving record of how he won it; Lita took it from him there, reversing a top-rope Lionsault into a rollup for the pin.

name: ZWF Eurocontinental Championship
epitaph: Chris Jericho's own second Summerslam title, defended the same night as his Light Heavyweight loss: he retained against Booker T, reversing a near-fall Bookend into a Bulldog and a Lionsault. The fed's own commentary names the belt "the Eurocontinental title"; the same broadcast separately introduces Booker T carrying "both Eurpean Title and Intercontinental Title," a wording the served text never reconciles.

name: ZWF Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The Rock carried the belt into ZWF Summerslam with no surviving record of how he won it, and retained it there against Supernova in a weapons brawl, winning with a second Rock Bottom through a table. The fed's own home page separately credits The Undertaker with a later Hardcore reign, its own origin equally unrecorded.

name: ZWF TV Championship
epitaph: X-Pac carried the belt into ZWF Summerslam with no surviving record of how he won it, and lost it there to Jeff Hardy in a Triple Threat also involving Zero, pinned by the Swanton Bomb after Hardy put Zero through a table. The fed's own home page separately credits The Undertaker with a later TV reign, its own origin — and the transition from Hardy's own Summerslam-won title — equally unrecorded.
